newsitem.title: USA: Bankers Trust Q2 revenue up in major units.
newsitem.headline: Bankers Trust Q2 revenue up in major units.

text.p: Bankers Trust New York Corp said Thursday revenue gains were broad-based in its global businesses, pushing second quarter net income to $181 million from $151 million in the same period a year ago, an increase of 20 percent.

"Compared to last year, revenue growth was especially strong in our trading and sales, investment banking and risk management services business units," chairman and chief executive Frank Newman said in a statement.

Bankers Trust said its Investment Banking business had net income of $113 million in the second quarter, up from $104 million a year ago and $96 million in the previous quarter. The increase over both periods reflected higher corporate finance income offset partly by higher personnel-related costs. Revenue from private equity investments declined from the high level of the second quarter of 1996 but increased slightly from the previous quarter.
Risk Management Services had net income of $7 million in the second quarter of 1997, up $25 million from the year-ago quarter and down $4 million from the previous quarter.
The 1996 second quarter in risk management services was hurt by losses in commodity derivatives when copper prices dropped sharply, Bankers Trust said.

Net income from the Trading and Sales business was $59 million, up $42 million from the second quarter of 1996 and $16 million from the first quarter of 1997. The improvement was largely due to strong arbitrage activities as compared to the prior year period and previous quarter.

The investment management business, which for reporting purposes does not include funds management activities in Australia and New Zealand, reported net income of $8 million for the current quarter, up $4 million from the 1996 comparable period due to improved performance fees. At June 30, 1997, assets under management in the unit were approximately $242 billion, compared to $206 billion at the end of the first quarter of 1997 and $191 billion a year ago.
Client processing services had $18 million of net income in the second quarter of 1997, down $2 million from the 1996 second quarter and up $5 million from the previous quarter.

The Asia business had a net loss of $14 million compared to net income of $7 million in the second quarter of 1996 and net income of $8 million in the previous quarter. Thailand is currently experiencing a significant reduction in its economic growth and the Thai stock market has experienced a steep decline, Bankers Trust said. As a result, Bankers Trust said it recognized a decline in value of its unconsolidated investment in a Thai finance company. Offsetting this decline, the Bankers Trust recognized trading gains from favorable Thai baht currency positions. The combined effect of these factors in Thailand resulted in a pre-tax net loss of $22 million.
The Australia/New Zealand business had net income of $23 million in the second quarter of 1997, down $10 million from the second quarter of 1996 and down $11 million from the previous quarter.

Latin America net income was $39 million in the second quarter of 1997, up $6 million from the second quarter of 1996 and up $16 million from the first quarter of 1997. A pre-tax gain of $22 million ($15 million after-tax) was recorded during the current quarter with the completion of the first stage on the sale of 50 percent of a stake in Consorcio, the largest life insurance and annuity firm in Chile.

Bankers Trust said total noninterest expenses for the second quarter of 1997 increased $203 million, or 25 percent, from the second quarter of 1996. Personnel-related expenses contributed $172 million to the increase. Salaries rose by $30 million due to growth in the number of employees and to annual pay increases.
Newman noted shareholders of Bankers Trust and Alex. Brown Inc will vote on their proposed August 13.
He said Bankers Trust approaches the merger with solid business momentum.
